title: The Room That Wasn't There
script: Guest: [thoughtful] I booked this room three months ago and paid in full. How exactly does a hotel run out of rooms that were already reserved?
Receptionist: I completely understand your frustration, and I'm sorry this has happened. Occasionally more rooms are reserved than we actually have available.
Guest: [carefully] That sounds like a problem you created, not one I should be expected to solve at eleven at night.
Receptionist: You're right, and it isn't your responsibility. What I can offer is a suite at a partner hotel two streets away, at no extra cost.
Guest: [reflective] A suite sounds like compensation dressed up as generosity. What's actually included, and how do I get there at this hour?
Receptionist: Breakfast, late checkout, and a taxi, all arranged and paid for by us. I can have the driver waiting within ten minutes.
Guest: [honestly] That's more reasonable than I expected, though I'd still like something for tomorrow, given the inconvenience tonight.
Receptionist: Understandably so. I can credit one night's stay back onto your original reservation once you return here tomorrow.
Guest: [gently] Provided the room tomorrow is actually available, unlike tonight's, I suppose that works.
Receptionist: I've personally confirmed it this time, rather than relying on the system, precisely because I don't want a repeat of this.
Guest: [calmly] I appreciate the honesty. It's more than most people offer when something's gone wrong on their end.
Receptionist: For what it's worth, this isn't how we like guests to be treated, and I've flagged it for the manager already.
Guest: [encouraging] Alright. I'll take the taxi and the suite, and we'll call it resolved, provided tomorrow goes smoothly.
Receptionist: Thank you for your patience. I'll text you the confirmation and the driver's details right away.
Guest: [seriously] Just make sure the suite actually exists, unlike this room apparently didn't.
Receptionist: I promise it does. I checked myself, twice, after tonight's mix-up.
Guest: Good. I'd rather trust you than the booking system, honestly.
Receptionist: A wise choice tonight. Safe trip across town, and I'll see you tomorrow.

quiz.question: What problem does the guest discover at check-in?
options: His card was declined
He booked the wrong dates
The hotel has no room for him despite his reservation
The hotel is under renovation
quiz.explanation: Despite booking and paying three months in advance, the hotel has run out of available rooms, a case of overbooking.

quiz.question: Why does the receptionist say the overbooking happened?
options: A computer virus deleted bookings
Occasionally more rooms are reserved than the hotel actually has available
The guest arrived too late
Another guest refused to leave
quiz.explanation: She explains that occasionally more rooms end up reserved than the hotel actually has available.

quiz.question: What does the receptionist offer as a solution for tonight?
options: A refund only
A suite at a partner hotel with breakfast, late checkout, and a paid taxi
A discount voucher for next time
A room to share with another guest
quiz.explanation: She offers a suite at a nearby partner hotel, with breakfast, late checkout, and a taxi all arranged and paid for.

quiz.question: What does the receptionist do differently to reassure the guest about tomorrow's room?
options: She upgrades him permanently
She calls the manager to apologise
She offers a full refund instead
She personally confirmed the room herself, rather than relying on the system
quiz.explanation: She says she personally confirmed tomorrow's room herself, rather than relying on the system, to avoid a repeat of the problem.

quiz.question: How does the guest's attitude change by the end of the conversation?
options: He remains angry and demands a refund
He cancels his stay entirely
He asks to speak to the manager
He softens and agrees to the arrangement, trusting the receptionist over the booking system
quiz.explanation: By the end, the guest relents, accepting the arrangement and saying he'd rather trust her than the booking system.

quiz.question: Why does the guest reject the partner hotel's suite as enough by itself?
options: Transport and practical access still matter late at night.
Within months, that single photograph had been shared thousands of times
My guest today has visited over ninety countries
He waved it off, saying he'd missed enough trains himself to know exactly how that particular panic feels
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: Transport and practical access still matter late at night.

quiz.question: What immediate arrangement does the receptionist make?
options: The hotel pays for a taxi arriving within ten minutes.
A fisherman I'd spoken to years earlier recognised me
I realised I could describe fifteen airports in vivid detail
Hospitals and trains, he said, both strip away pretence
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: The hotel pays for a taxi arriving within ten minutes.

quiz.question: Which compensation addresses the disruption beyond relocation?
options: I asked him whether he wished I'd never taken the picture
Fewer destinations per trip, for a start
One night will be credited back to the reservation.
He texted a month later, simply to say his father had recovered
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: One night will be credited back to the reservation.

quiz.question: How does the receptionist reduce the risk of another failed booking?
options: I still photograph places I love
Missing something is preferable to remembering nothing clearly
She personally confirms the replacement room instead of trusting the system.
I got the job, as it happens
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: She personally confirms the replacement room instead of trusting the system.

quiz.question: What information will the guest receive before leaving?
options: The village will keep changing regardless of what I do
A written confirmation and the driver's details.
Thank you for joining us today
A stranger wedged his bag into the door gap and held it until she caught up
quiz.explanation: This matches the audio: A written confirmation and the driver's details.
